proposed.summary: The onboarding ended blocked (decision) at validate: the secrets check rejected two map documents for url-userinfo, INTEGRATIONS.md:56 and CONCERNS.md:118. Both quote the repository own development default `postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/recipecart` from src/platform/config.ts (a placeholder credential, not a secret, but a credential-bearing URL). The gate worked as designed, the harness is sound (digests equal, 0 containment findings, 0.1174 USD, 1 invocation, no knowledge pass reached), and the repository and the model are not at fault. The product defect is that the mapper contract does not tell the mapper to omit or redact connection strings with userinfo, so an ordinary repository with a documented dev DSN is blocked at map validation. Candidate rulings for the owner: (a) add a mapper rule (never write a URL with user:password userinfo; name the setting and the file instead) and re-run GroceriesGPT once (about 0.6 to 1.0 USD); (b) offer the existing decision (accept the documents) for a placeholder credential and re-run; (c) accept GroceriesGPT as a documented blocked outcome (the pass bar of AC-14 is 5 of 5, so this fails the bar).

stops.summary: The onboarding ended active with equal digests and 0 containment failures, but the knowledge index is absent (budget_exhausted), so the repository is not active with the knowledge pass. Under owner ruling 2 the corpus was capped to 12 chunks (50 of 181 documents kept, 131 left out as cost-cap; per-invocation cap 0.8 USD). The knowledge session read and wrote all 12 chunk files (each parses; 12 of 12), answered "done", and ended at 0.8058 USD, 0.0058 over its 0.8 USD cap (67 turns, 6.07M tokens): the host reported error_max_budget_usd, the invocation was classified budget_exhausted, and the stage discards the written chunks for that ending. The same 12-chunk limit passed on auto_search_workflow (knowledge 0.7518 USD, 41 documents). Measured per-session cost is superlinear in chunks: 6 chunks 0.302 USD (attempt 1), 12 chunks 0.752 to 0.806 USD, so the 0.05 USD a chunk and 0.75 share of the cap overstate how many chunks fit; a quadratic through those points (0.0328 n + 0.00286 n^2) gives about 9 chunks at 0.6 USD and 10 at 0.8 USD x 0.75 headroom.

proposedClassification.summary: The calibration of the corpus cap (the per-chunk cost constant and the cap share in src/domain/knowledge-corpus.ts, KNOWLEDGE_COST) is too optimistic for the portfolio corpus, so the invocation overran its own cap by 0.7 percent and lost 12 complete chunk files. Not a harness defect: the tool, digests and containment are fine. Candidate rulings for the owner: (a) recalibrate the constants to the measured curve (about 9 chunks at 0.8 USD) and re-run the portfolio once; (b) keep the limit and also accept a budget_exhausted ending when every planned chunk file is written and usable (this changes how an ending is classified, which ruling 2 did not choose); (c) both.
